Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-medium-0009", "row_sha256": "0788ea0354ce5668b17fd4b07936459abc6c1b043606c610aa1ca47beba34a61", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "write a short, practical procedure for staff at a ferry luggage desk for bags that passengers hand in, and keep it limited to sorting and recording those bags. for each bag, first check whether its name tag is readable. if there is a readable name tag, put the bag on the tagged-bag shelf and write down the passenger name shown on the tag. if the name tag is missing or can't be read, don't put it on that shelf; keep the bag at the luggage desk and write down a brief description of the bag instead. those are the two alternatives, so don't treat an unreadable tag like a readable one or tell staff to do both sets of steps. make the steps easy to follow when several bags arrive, but don't add a passenger-contact step, an unprovided storage location, or a rule for what happens later. use plain language and say which action goes with each condition. the procedure should cover only the handling and record entry described here, not a larger lost-property policy. use a brief heading and numbered steps if that helps the staff follow it quickly. could you make this into a concise staff procedure with the condition and the other option easy to distinguish?", "output": "Draft a concise, practical procedure for staff at a ferry luggage desk covering only the sorting and recording of bags passengers hand in. Use plain language, with a brief heading and numbered steps if helpful. Explain what to do for each bag, including when several bags arrive.

Make the two alternatives clear:
- If a bag has a readable name tag, place it on the tagged-bag shelf and record the passenger name shown on the tag.
- If the tag is missing or unreadable, keep the bag at the luggage desk and record a brief description of the bag instead. Do not direct staff to use the readable-tag steps for this case or to carry out both sets of steps.

Keep the procedure limited to the handling and record entry described above. Do not add a passenger-contact step, another storage location, a later action, or broader lost-property policy."}]
